nodes.title: bulk-reader
nodes.summary: Reads large files, many files, logs or long diffs in its own disposable context and returns only a compact answer. Use instead of reading files >350 lines or 3+ files into the main context. Give it a precise question and the paths.

nodes.title: claude-md-compliance-checker
nodes.summary: Checks recent changes against CLAUDE.md, docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md and docs/policies/*. Use after process-relevant changes (new files/structure, deploy, docs, tests) or when drift is suspected; cheap.

nodes.title: code-quality-pragmatist
nodes.summary: Flags over-engineering, needless abstraction and premature optimisation relative to the project's rigor level. Use after a feature or design lands, especially at L0–L2.

nodes.title: code-writer
nodes.summary: Generates boilerplate (tests, CRUD, config, fixtures, migrations, repetitive variants) that follows an existing reference file. Use when the spec is clear and a pattern exists to copy; not for design decisions or debugging.

nodes.title: data-builder
nodes.summary: Heavy-lifting builder for spreadsheets, workbooks, CSV/data pipelines and generated reports. Builds them with scripts (Python openpyxl/pandas) so the output is reproducible, verifiable and cheap to regenerate. Use for the data-spreadsheet path.

nodes.title: deploy-watcher
nodes.summary: Watches a git-triggered Cloudflare build in the background until the new version is live (or a bounded timeout), smoke-checks it, records push-to-live time, and reports one line. Always launch with run_in_background so the main agent keeps working instead of waiting on git, CI or Cloudflare.

nodes.title: developer
nodes.summary: Implements a backlog item end to end (code + tests + docs touch-ups) following docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md, the design/ADRs and the spec. Use for well-specified feature work that can run in its own context (e.g. parallel slices, or to keep the main context free); the main agent stays the coordinator. For pure boilerplate use code-writer instead.

nodes.title: doc-keeper
nodes.summary: Updates project documentation after a change — docs/, ADRs, README, CLAUDE.md quick facts and the curated block of docs/INDEX.md. Use at the end of every task that changed behaviour, commands, structure or decisions.

nodes.title: jenny
nodes.summary: Spec-vs-implementation auditor. Checks that what was built matches docs/GOAL.md, the spec and acceptance criteria. Use at milestone end or when you suspect requirement gaps; not for per-task checks.

nodes.title: karen
nodes.summary: Reality check on claimed completion: runs the thing and reports what actually works vs what is marked done (BACKLOG.md, dashboard). Use before declaring a milestone done or when progress claims smell optimistic.

nodes.title: product-manager
nodes.summary: Product owner for the project. Turns GOAL.md into a prioritised backlog, milestones, user stories with acceptance criteria and scope cuts; challenges value and scope. Use when planning milestones, refining the backlog, writing specs, or deciding what NOT to build. Does not write code.

nodes.title: reviewer
nodes.summary: Independent fresh-context review of a change against GOAL.md, OPERATING-MODEL.md and the active path's quality gates. Use before merging or declaring a milestone done. It did not write the code, so it is not anchored on the author's reasoning.

nodes.title: software-architect
nodes.summary: Designs the technical shape of software: components, boundaries, data model, APIs, Cloudflare products, testing strategy, and the trade-offs, recorded as ADRs. Use at the start of the software-product/library-cli/infra-ops paths, before a large or risky feature, or when a design is in question. Expensive; not for routine tasks.

nodes.title: spreadsheet-architect
nodes.summary: Designs spreadsheet and data models before anything is built: sheets, inputs vs calculations vs outputs, formulas, named ranges, validation, checks and the generator layout that data-builder then implements. Use at the start of the data-spreadsheet path or before restructuring a workbook or financial/data model.

nodes.title: task-completion-validator
nodes.summary: Verifies one claimed task is functionally complete (not stubbed, mocked or half-wired) against its acceptance criteria. Use at the end of a non-trivial task at rigor L2+, before ticking it in BACKLOG.md.

nodes.title: test-runner
nodes.summary: Runs tests/builds/linters and returns only the verdict, timing and the minimal failure detail. Use for any command whose output may be long, so logs never enter the main context.

nodes.title: ui-comprehensive-tester
nodes.summary: End-to-end UI testing of web/mobile interfaces (Playwright preferred; it is pre-installed in cloud sessions). Use when a change touches user-facing UI or flows; tests against a preview URL or local server.

nodes.title: ultrathink-debugger
nodes.summary: Deep root-cause debugging for hard bugs, production issues and mysterious failures. Expensive (Opus): use only after one normal debugging attempt failed or for production incidents.

nodes.title: Brainstorm — agree the goal
nodes.summary: Phase 1. Interview the user about what they want to build, sharpen it into an agreed goal, and write docs/GOAL.md. Use at the start of a new project (factory.json phase "brainstorm"), when the user says "let's start", or when the goal changes materially.

nodes.title: Choose path — pick the operating model
nodes.summary: Phase 2. Walk the decision tree with the agreed goal, pick the operating model (primary + optional secondary path), and write docs/OPERATING-MODEL.md with the agents, practices, habits, policies, commands and budgets for this project. Use after brainstorm, or when the project's nature changes.

nodes.title: Dashboard
nodes.summary: Build and show the project dashboard — versions, phase and progress, backlog state, tech debt, key metrics (tests, coverage, deploys, tokens), alerts. Use when the user asks for status, progress, a dashboard, "where are we", or after a milestone, release or retro.

nodes.title: Docs sync
nodes.summary: Bring documentation up to date with the code after a change, and regenerate the docs index and knowledge graph. Use at the end of any task that changed behaviour, commands, structure or decisions, or when the user says "update docs".

nodes.title: Metrics
nodes.summary: Record and review delivery metrics — test time, coverage, deploy duration/failures, token spend per session — and suggest structural improvements to cut wait time and token cost. Use when the user asks about speed, coverage, cost, CI time, or after changing test/deploy setup.

nodes.title: Retro — keep the factory learning
nodes.summary: Milestone retrospective. Reviews metrics (test time, coverage, deploys, tokens), what slowed us down or cost tokens, and enriches the decision tree, path playbooks and LEARNINGS.md so the next project starts smarter. Use at milestones, after a painful session, or when the user says "retro" or "what did we learn".

nodes.title: Security audit (on request)
nodes.summary: On-request security audit using Cloudflare's security-audit skill (installed on demand). Use only when the user explicitly asks for a security audit, pen-test, vulnerability review, or before an L3 release per OPERATING-MODEL.md. Not run automatically.

nodes.title: Ship — git-based, asynchronous deploys to Cloudflare
nodes.summary: Take software live on Cloudflare via git, without waiting on it. Push to the production branch -> Cloudflare builds and deploys; PR branches -> preview URLs; a background deploy-watcher confirms and records it. Use when software needs to go live, for first-time Cloudflare setup, previews, slow deploys, or a failed deploy. Loads the cloudflare-deploy reference skill on demand.

nodes.title: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Always-loaded instructions. Keep short and stable (it is paid every turn). Details live in docs/ — find them via docs/INDEX.md.

nodes.title: danfactory
nodes.summary: A template for starting Claude Code projects. It gives you a guided start (brainstorm → decision tree → operating model), saves tokens by design, keeps the docs indexed, tracks delivery metrics, runs security audits on request, and deploys to Cloudflare via git.

nodes.title: Backlog
nodes.summary: Milestones and work items; the dashboard reads this file. Seeded by `choose-path`, ticked off as part of every task's definition of done.

nodes.title: Goal
nodes.summary: The agreed goal for this project. Written by the `brainstorm` skill after the user confirms. Keep under ~80 lines.

nodes.title: Operating model
nodes.summary: How this project is built: chosen path(s), rigor, agents, practices, gates, budgets. Written by the `choose-path` skill; revised by `retro`.

nodes.title: Tech debt register
nodes.summary: Known shortcuts and their cost; the dashboard reads this file plus automated signals (TODO/FIXME markers, oversized files, import cycles). Updated by `retro` and `engineering:tech-debt` audits.

nodes.title: NNNN — Title
nodes.summary: Status: proposed | accepted | superseded by NNNN · Date: YYYY-MM-DD

nodes.title: 0001 — Start from the danfactory template
nodes.summary: Status: accepted · Date: 2026-11-06

nodes.title: Agent routing
nodes.summary: Which agent gets involved when. The main agent coordinates and decides; subagents are delegated to only when they save tokens or time, or add independence. Enriched by `retro`.

nodes.title: Decision tree
nodes.summary: Picks the operating model for a goal. Version 1.0.0. Keep this file short: details live in paths/*.md. Enriched by `retro` from LEARNINGS.md.

nodes.title: Learnings
nodes.summary: Append-only log written by `retro`. Each entry tags path(s) and a type; `[upstream]` entries should be copied back to the template repo.

nodes.title: Path: automation-script
nodes.summary: Glue code, integrations, scheduled jobs, bots, one-purpose scripts. Default rigor L1.

nodes.title: Path: data-spreadsheet
nodes.summary: Spreadsheets, financial/data models, workbooks, CSV outputs, generated reports. Default rigor L1 (L2 if decisions/money depend on it). **Heavy lifting by scripts and agents, never cell-by-cell in chat.**

nodes.title: Path: documents-content
nodes.summary: Documents, decks, handbooks, proposals, long-form writing. Default rigor L1.

nodes.title: Path: infra-ops
nodes.summary: Infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, cloud config, DNS, access. Default rigor L3 (blast radius).

nodes.title: Path: library-cli
nodes.summary: Packages, SDKs, CLIs that others import or invoke. Default rigor L2.

nodes.title: Path: prototype-spike
nodes.summary: Throwaway code to learn or prove feasibility. Rigor L0. Speed over polish — but time-boxed.

nodes.title: Path: research-analysis
nodes.summary: Questions answered from sources or data: market scans, technical comparisons, data analysis. Default rigor L1.

nodes.title: Path: software-product
nodes.summary: Apps, APIs, services with users. Default rigor L2 (L3 if money/PII/public). Goes live via git → Cloudflare (`ship`).

nodes.title: Policy: asynchronous delivery (no waiting on git, CI or Cloudflare)
nodes.summary: The agent's time is the most expensive part of a deploy. Push, hand off, keep working; builds are made short by design and every wait is bounded.

nodes.title: Policy: documentation
nodes.summary: Docs are part of done. Small, true, linked — and indexed so agents never read more than they need.

nodes.title: Policy: security
nodes.summary: Secure defaults always; full audits on request or before L3 releases.

nodes.title: Policy: testing and delivery metrics
nodes.summary: Fast feedback is a feature. Measure test time, coverage, deploys and tokens; act on the trend.

nodes.title: Policy: token economy
nodes.summary: Spend tokens on decisions, not on moving bytes. Adapted from Spotify's `shunt` plugin (delegate I/O-heavy work to a cheaper worker) using native Claude Code subagents.
